name: Detect OSS vs Enterprise by Auth Before Setting Up an LLM Provider (Custom Domain)
query: Our Conductor server is at https://conductor.acme.internal/api. I want our workflows to use OpenAI gpt-4o-mini — set that up. My OpenAI key is exported as OPENAI_API_KEY.
expected_behavior: Step 1: The hostname doesn't say whether this is OSS or Orkes, so determine it from the server (SKILL.md Rule 17): `python3 "$CONDUCTOR_API" server-info` (no credentials sent) or an unauthenticated `conductor workflow list`

Step 2: If auth is required (401/403) → Enterprise/Orkes: set CONDUCTOR_SERVER_TYPE=Enterprise, authenticate with injected key/secret, then follow the integration flow — integration-list, integration-save with --config-env api_key=OPENAI_API_KEY (after confirming), model-sync / model-save, access, and `llmProvider` = the integration name

Step 3: If no auth is required → OSS: OpenAI is enabled by setting OPENAI_API_KEY in the Conductor *server's* environment (restart the server), `llmProvider: openai`; integration APIs don't exist on OSS, so don't call them
Step 4: Verify with a one-task LLM_CHAT_COMPLETE test workflow written to a file
success_criteria: Determines OSS vs Enterprise from whether the server requires auth (`server-info`, or an unauthenticated request returning 401/403 vs success) before choosing a setup path
Does not decide the flavor from the hostname / URL alone

Enterprise branch: uses the integration flow (integration-save with the key from the env var, model registration, `llmProvider` = the integration name) and sets/mentions CONDUCTOR_SERVER_TYPE=Enterprise
OSS branch: sets OPENAI_API_KEY in the Conductor server's environment and uses `llmProvider: openai`, without calling integration APIs
The OpenAI key value never appears in chat or a command argument
Does not fall back to an HTTP task calling api.openai.com
